Rs.1500 Prize Bond - Pattern Audit

Draws 80-107 (2019-11-15 to 2026-08-17) · 47,600 winning numbers · 74 tests · 10,000 Monte Carlo histories · generated 2026-10-08 13:11

Is there an exploitable pattern? No.

Confidence: high. 12 descriptive tests remain significant after correction, and all of them measure one thing: inside a single draw, the winners are slightly clumped. Some draws are lumpier than a perfectly uniform draw would be. The clumps land in different places every draw, and no rule built on any pattern beat random picks out of sample, so this cannot be used to predict winners. Of 74 tests, 20 had a nominal p-value below 0.05. By luck alone about 3.7 would. After Benjamini-Hochberg correction, 12 remain significant. In the walk-forward backtest (draws 91-107, 17 out-of-sample draws, 1,000 picks per draw), random picks would be expected to win 28.9 times. The best rule, "Repeat last draw's winners", won 32 times (one-sided p=0.308 before correction). No rule beats chance, so no prediction is better than picking numbers at random.

1 · Executive summary

  • Repeat winners: 1,036 numbers have won in more than one draw, against about 1,061 expected by chance (p=0.4284, corrected 0.7731). Total repeats: 1,072 vs 1,093 expected (p=0.5423, corrected 0.8574). Repeats at every lag (1-10 draws apart), and 1st/2nd prize numbers winning again, are within the range expected by chance. Drawing about 1,700 numbers out of 1,000,000 every quarter produces about this many repeats. They are not a pattern.
  • Within-draw clustering - the one statistically real finding. Inside a single draw, the 3rd-prize numbers are slightly more clumped than uniform random numbers. There are 911 gaps of 10 or less between consecutive winners, against 799 expected. Range counts are over-dispersed by about 7% at the 1,000-wide scale and 12% at the 10,000-wide scale. Most of it comes from a few draws, especially 104, 102, 103, 88 (see section 4). Without draw 104, the small-gap test gives 848 vs 770 (p=0.0057, corrected 0.0349) and the bucket test gives p=0.0100, corrected 0.0570. The clumps fall in different places each draw (between-draw stability p=0.0002, corrected 0.0025; first-half vs second-half range correlation r=+0.011). So the clustering does not say where the next draw's winners will be. It probably reflects how the draw is generated or batched, but these files cannot show the mechanism.
  • Digits and ranges: Significant after correction: Digit frequency, position 1 (chi2=23.8 (max dev 5.5%), corrected p=0.0322); Digit frequency, position 2 (chi2=24.5 (max dev 4.5%), corrected p=0.0295); Digit frequency, all positions pooled (chi2=86.6, corrected p=0.0295); First two digits (100 ranges of 10,000) (chi2=139; busiest=59 (534), corrected p=0.0322); Stability of first-two-digit ranges across draws (chi2=2945, corrected p=0.0025). These are most likely a side effect of the clustering above. A clumped draw puts extra winners into whichever ranges its clumps fall in, and the pooled tests assume independent numbers. The over-represented ranges do not persist: ranges that were busy in the first half of the history were not busy in the second half. Every other digit test (endings, digit sum, odd/even, repeated digits, palindromes) is consistent with chance.
  • Between draws: significant after correction: Per-draw mean off-centre (chi2=52.7, corrected p=0.0295). This is driven by draw 85, whose winners lean toward low numbers (z=-4.0). Without that draw, p=0.0998. The direction varies between draws (no drift in mean, median or spread), so this is the same draw-level lumpiness, not a usable bias. The other between-draw tests (nearby numbers in the next draw, 1st prize vs 2nd/3rd prizes, drift over time) are consistent with chance unless listed here.
  • Folklore (hot numbers, overdue numbers, 'due' ranges, lucky endings, 786, round and 'fancy' numbers): none is supported by the data.
  • Prediction (out of sample): 8 rules picking 1,000 numbers per draw scored between 19 and 32 hits. Random picks would be expected to score 28.9 (95% range 19-40). The higher-power version, which bets on the 10 hottest 10,000-ranges (10% of all numbers), caught 10.23% of later winners against 10.00% for random (one-sided p=0.0998; 95% CI for the lift x0.99-x1.06). No rule beats chance. No prediction is better than picking numbers at random.
  • Actual odds (latest draw, 1,700 winners): a given 6-digit number wins any prize with probability 0.170% per draw (1 in 588), or about 0.68% per year (4 draws). 1st prize: 1 in 1,000,000. 2nd: 1 in 333,333. 3rd: 1 in 590. At the listed prize amounts, the gross expected payout is about Rs.37.4 per Rs.1500 bond per draw (≈2.5% per draw, before withholding tax). It is the same for every number.

2 · Data validation (Step 1)

28 files parsed into draws_clean.csv (47,600 rows; numbers kept as 6-character strings). Missing draw numbers: none. Malformed tokens: 0. Duplicates within a draw: 0. The 3rd-prize list is in ascending order in 28/28 files. Days between draws: 87-94 (median 92). Every draw has 1 first prize, 3 second prizes and the same number of third prizes. Some files label the prizes differently (18500- or 3000000-Prize-1 instead of 18500- Prize - 3). The parser therefore reads the tier from the prize amount, not from the label.

3 · Results table (Steps 2 & 3)

The null hypothesis is that each draw picks its winners uniformly at random from 000000-999999, independently of other draws. "Expected" values come from 10,000 simulated histories with the same draw sizes (mean and 95% range) or from exact/analytic distributions. All 74 p-values are two-sided, except the backtest, which is one-sided ("beats random"). They are corrected together with Benjamini-Hochberg, and a Bonferroni column is also shown. Highlighted rows remain significant after correction.

4 · Where the within-draw clustering is

Per-draw clustering diagnostics for the 3rd-prize list. If the winners were uniformly random, each draw would have about 28.5 gaps of 10 or less, a 100-bucket chi-square around 99 and a variance/mean ratio around 1.0. Most draws are ordinary. A few are clearly clumpier, and their clumps are in different places each time.

5 · Charts

6 · Backtest detail (Step 3)

For each training end-draw t = 90..106, each rule uses only draws 80..t to choose exactly 1,000 numbers. Hits are then counted in draw t+1. For random picks, the hits in a draw follow a hypergeometric distribution. The total over all test draws is simulated 200,000 times, giving 28.9 expected (95% range 19-40). The "hits / expected" column is the effect size: 1.00 means no better than random. With only about 29 expected hits, these 1,000-number tests can detect only a large edge. A higher-power variant therefore bets on the 10 historically hottest 10,000-ranges (100,000 numbers). Across the same test draws it caught 2,956 of 28,900 winners (10.23% vs 10.00% expected; one-sided p=0.0998; 95% CI for the lift x0.988-x1.058).

8 · Limitations

  • Sample size. 28 draws (about 47,600 numbers) is plenty for digit and range tests. It is small for draw-to-draw tests and for the backtest (17 out-of-sample draws, ≈29 expected hits per rule). A rule would need to roughly double the hit rate to be detected reliably (≈80% power), so a very small edge cannot be ruled out. Even if one existed, it could not overcome the house odds.
  • Series are not recorded. The same 6-digit number exists in many series, and these files list only the number. All analysis is at the number level. Whether a prize is paid in one series or all of them does not change any test here.
  • The draw method may have changed over 2019-2026 (machine, software or the number range in circulation). A change that kept the output uniform would not show up in these tests. A change that broke uniformity would show up in the stability/drift tests, and it does not.
  • Number range. The null assumes all of 000000-999999 is eligible. The bucket tests show the winners cover that whole range evenly, which supports the assumption.
  • Multiple testing. 74 tests at p<0.05 would produce about 3.7 false positives by luck. That is why the corrected p-values decide the conclusions.

Reproduce: python3 analysis.py (add raw/108.csv and re-run). Seed 20261008.
